project.name: charlie-backend
project.description: FastAPI backend with JWT authentication, role-based access control, SQLAlchemy persistence, and auth event logging.

edges.summary: Main application includes the auth router.
App metadata and middleware configuration come from settings.
App startup relies on shared database session wiring indirectly through the router stack.
Route handlers forward requests to the controller.
Role-protected routes use the shared RBAC dependency.
/auth/me uses the current-user dependency from token service.
RBAC dependency resolves the current user through token validation.
RBAC dependency delegates role parsing and permission checks to domain rules.
Controller delegates all use cases to the auth service.
Registration and login load or create users through the repository.
Login, refresh, and logout persist or revoke refresh tokens through the repository.
Registration hashes passwords and login verifies them.
Service uses token helpers to mint access and refresh tokens and verify refresh tokens.
Registration parses the requested role and role endpoints reuse domain role checks.
Service emits auth domain events after each use case.
Access and refresh expiration windows come from settings.
Refresh-token validation and persistence use token repository primitives.
Current-user resolution loads the user row by ID.
JWT signing and expiry windows use application settings.
The public get_current_user dependency resolves a DB session through get_db.
Password hashing feeds user persistence during registration.
User repository persists and queries the User ORM model.
Token repository persists and queries the Token ORM model.
Role validation is based on the shared enum.
The ORM role column stores the canonical enum.
Auth events are the dispatcher payloads.
Dispatcher routes each event to the logging listener.
The implementation review explains the event and token lifecycle this listener observes.
End-to-end tests exercise register/login/refresh/logout/me and role-protected routes.
Unit tests validate role parsing and invalid-role rejection.
Tests confirm auth events dispatch to registered listeners.
Tests override the database dependency with an in-memory SQLite session.
Migration creates the tables modeled by the ORM.
Migration aligns the schema with the cleaned-up auth models.
Project README describes the backend at a high level.
Review notes describe the register/login/refresh/logout sequence in the service.
